children: Chicago Board of Trade corn futures fell on Tuesday as traders waited to see whether China may buy US farm goods in conjunction with planned talks between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping this week, analysts said.
Trump will welcome the Chinese leader at the White House for their second meeting this year, as the two leaders seek stability in a relationship under pressure over trade and other issues.
CBOT grain and soy futures eased after rallying on Monday in anticipation of the summit.
The U.S. corn harvest is underway, though rain is delaying progress in some areas, analysts said.
After trading ended on Monday, the US Department of Agriculture reported the corn harvest was 13% complete as of Sunday and soybeans were 12% harvested, ahead of their five-year averages.
CBOT December corn (CZ26) ended down 6-1/4 cents at $5.36-3/4 per bushel.
